seam_gaps.hazard: Adjacent terrain tiles decimated independently will show cracks or T-junctions at their shared edges unless edge vertices are shared exactly.

float_jitter.hazard: float32 vertices relative to an ENU origin 2-3 km away will cause visible jitter or z-fighting at the scales used.

geoid_const.hazard: Using one constant geoid offset over a 4 km alpine site introduces height errors larger than 10 cm.

building_float.hazard: LoD2 buildings placed on a 4 m decimated terrain will float above or sink into the ground by more than 1 m on steep slopes.

road_drape.hazard: Road ribbons draped at 0.3 m over a 4 m terrain mesh will cut into or hover over the terrain on cliffs and embankments.

odbl.hazard: Mixing ODbL OpenStreetMap data into the same derived tiles as swisstopo data creates share-alike obligations for the combined database.

public_leak.hazard: Serving tiles from the Next.js public folder risks exposing them without the password gate.

texture_mem.hazard: Sixteen 4000x4000 JPEG textures will exceed typical browser GPU memory budgets on laptops.

determinism.hazard: Pipeline output digests will not be deterministic across runs because of floating-point or library ordering differences.

truth_leak.hazard: Using swissBUILDINGS3D as the measured building layer in milestone 1 makes it harder to keep it hidden from the deduction engine in milestone 2.
